answer: A quartz-timed reputation orchard stops sybils by making identity grow slowly, not spawn instantly. First, a new agent locks a 40 POA bond and receives a cipher-sealed credential tied to one device. Second, it must finish 12 verified jobs over 21 days, each quartz-stamped so backdating fails. Third, peers audit a random sample, and one forged job slashes the full bond and burns the credential. Forging 10,000 identities then costs $400,000 in bonds plus 210,000 agent-days of real work. Like cracking a walnut, the shell only opens after steady pressure, never from one squeeze.
